summary: WorldEntity generation-8 candidate PR #429 bounds per-record state, canonical metadata, duplicate-diagnostic count, and retained duplicate-diagnostic bytes, but its closure-private registry can still retain an unbounded number of unique canonical records. createRegistry() owns no record-population budget; each successful unique register() inserts another immutable record, and count() traverses the full retained population. Because the architecture defines this registry as an in-memory identity/lifecycle index rather than the universe database, the absence of a project-owned population envelope leaves memory retention and count work caller-unbounded.
evidence: Inspected current WorldEntity generation-8 candidate PR #429 exact head a5374aadce95ee0c3992c75d81b1d9b8619d0e7d rather than stale main source.

At that head, createRegistry accepts only duplicateDiagnosticCapacity; records is a closure-private table with no configured or source-owned maximum unique-record count, and successful register assigns records[ownedRecord.id] = ownedRecord without a population preflight.
Registry count() iterates every retained record, so both retained memory and count work scale without a project-owned upper bound as callers register additional unique IDs.
Docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explicitly describes the WorldEntity registry as an in-memory identity/lifecycle index and diagnostic guard, not the universe database or persistence repository.

Duplicate screening covered open WorldEntity PRs/issues and today's 2026-08-12 control events. Existing WorldEntity work covers state depth/nodes/string bytes, duplicate-diagnostic capacity/bytes, canonical metadata bytes, hostile identities/revisions, and origin-complete duplicate diagnostics; no active finding or PR was found for unique registry population capacity.

FidelityManager PR #419 establishes the adjacent project pattern: caller-configurable registration still requires a source-owned safety ceiling so a finite caller value cannot effectively remove the memory/state envelope.
This is source-only capacity analysis; no Roblox Studio, viewport, physical-contact, performance-target, or two-client evidence is claimed.

metadata.recommendedNext: In the active HG-BACKFILL-WORLDENTITY lineage, add an explicit registry population budget with a project-owned upper safety ceiling rather than an arbitrary effectively-unbounded finite value. Reject the first unique registration beyond capacity before records mutation, keep duplicate-first-authority semantics unchanged, prove rejection is fail-atomic, prove unregister releases capacity, preserve valid retry, and test with a deliberately small configured budget so no large allocation is required. Choose/document the production default or required caller budget from active-authority design rather than treating the safety ceiling as a performance target.
